name: Connected Wi-Fi name and BSSID
plain: Reads the name and ID of the Wi-Fi network the phone is on, which gives away place.
meaning: SSID and BSSID are lookup keys for geolocation databases, so apps need location permission to read them.

android.permission: ACCESS_WIFI_STATE (normal) plus ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION; NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES (API 33) for scans
android.store_policy: Play: location policy applies to Wi-Fi scanning
android.note: Location services must be on; SSID returns <unknown ssid> without grant; scan throttle 4 scans per 2 minutes foreground

ios.permission: com.apple.developer.networking.wifi-info plus Precise Location (iOS 13), or hotspot config, VPN or MDM
ios.prompt_ui: Precise location prompt; Wi-Fi Info capability in Xcode
ios.note: Without entitlement and location the call returns nil

limits.headline: Can see your Wi-Fi name, but only with location access and extra approval
limits.user_action: You tap Allow Location when the app asks to see your Wi-Fi
can: See the Wi-Fi name (SSID) and BSSID on Android after Location is allowed
See the current Wi-Fi name on iPhone with the entitlement and Precise Location
Use the Wi-Fi name to guess a place such as home or work
cannot: See the name on Android when Location services are off (you get unknown ssid)
See the name on iPhone without the Apple entitlement and Precise Location
Scan more than 4 times per 2 minutes in the foreground on Android
Get the name if you decline Location
limits.differs: Android needs a Location grant. iPhone needs a special Apple entitlement plus Precise Location, or hotspot, VPN or MDM role.

story.what_it_is: An app can read the name and ID of your Wi-Fi network, which gives away where you are.
story.for_you: You see a location prompt if an app wants to read your Wi-Fi name. If you allow it, the app can tell whether you are at home or in a cafe. If you deny it, the name comes back as unknown.
story.for_makers: Makers need the name for device setup and diagnostics. The router ID can be looked up in a database to find a street address, so platforms put it behind the location permission.

use_cases.example: A smart bulb app reads your home Wi-Fi name so it can send it to the new bulb.
A Wi-Fi tool shows the name, channel and speed of the network you are on.
A hotel app notices you joined the hotel Wi-Fi and shows a welcome screen.
A work app turns on features only at the office network.
A data broker reads the router ID and looks up your street address in a database.
A security tool warns you when you join an open network with a familiar name that has a new ID.

story.android_note: Android hides the network name unless the app has location permission and location is on.
story.ios_note: iPhone needs the Access Wi-Fi Information entitlement and location permission to read it.

technical_bounds: Apple requires both entitlement and location
Android requires location services to be on
iOS needs an entitlement Apple must approve
